sections.content: How many people are "actors, entertainers and presenters"?

47,245 people

were counted on the census as "actors, entertainers and presenters" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Actors, entertainers and presenters may sing, portray roles in dramatic productions, perform comedy routines, gymnastic feats and tricks of illusion, train animals to perform and perform with them, and introduce and present radio and television programmes. This category includes Youtubers and social media influencers.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "actors, entertainers and presenters", 17.4% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "actors, entertainers and presenters" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "actors, entertainers and presenters" included:

  • business sales executives
  • sales related occupations (other)
  • agricultural and fishing trades (other)

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

A similar number of men and women had this job

Among people working as "actors, entertainers and presenters" there were a similar number of men and women (51.8% compared with 48.2%).

This means "actors, entertainers and presenters" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "culture, media and sports occupations".

Men made up 51.8% and women made up 48.2% of "actors, entertainers and presenters"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "actors, entertainers and presenters" included:

  • importers and exporters
  • higher education teaching professionals
  • horticultural trades

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "actors, entertainers and presenters" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "actors, entertainers and presenters" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "actors, entertainers and presenters", 12.8% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work part-time than full-time (64.2% compared with 35.8%).

They are also more likely to be self-employed (84.5%) than an employee (15.5%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Lambeth, this is in the same region of London.
